summary: Backend API testing complete for KG Vac Service - Job Manager. 46/46 pytest tests passed covering auth (login/me/forgot-password/change-password), RBAC enforcement (staff 403 on admin endpoints), customers CRUD, categories CRUD, jobs CRUD + filters + search + role scoping, status workflow (Scheduled->Start->Processing->Completed, Rescheduled with date/time + activity log, Cancelled with reason + reminders suppression), dashboard stats (role-scoped), earnings (completed-only, role-scoped, by_staff/by_category breakdowns for admin), notifications (list/mark-read/mark-all-read + assignment notification), and user management (create with must_change_password=true, duplicate email 400, disable user blocks login, admin-initiated reset-password returns ok). Tests had to be run with `-n 0` (serial) since the shared-state design is incompatible with the default `-n 2 --dist loadscope` xdist config in pytest.ini; the main agent should either keep running serially or add class-scoped auth fixtures if parallel is required.

minor.issue: Reschedule accepted without a 'note' field in StatusChangeIn validator defaults ('' allowed); minor UX only — functionality works as specified.
Returns all users (including admin) to staff; spec says staff see only own jobs/earnings but user list is intentionally shared for name lookup. Acceptable, but worth confirming with product.

action_items: Backend is fully functional against the external preview URL. Main agent can proceed with frontend implementation/testing.

Note: pytest.ini forces `-n 2 --dist loadscope` which breaks module-level shared STATE across classes. Current tests run with `-n 0`. If parallel execution is required later, refactor shared STATE into class-scoped fixtures.
Email send via Emergent Resend may fail (503) under real send attempts, but endpoints correctly return ok=true and persist tokens to db.password_reset_tokens — verified.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~960 lines — above the 700-line soft guideline. Consider splitting into modules (auth, jobs, customers, notifications, scheduler, email).

list_jobs: when both `date_from/date_to` and `q` are provided, `query['$or']` is set, which could silently combine with `query['scheduled_at']` as AND (which is fine), but the custom-id regex match on `id` scans the collection — acceptable at this scale.
reminder_loop runs forever with 60s cadence; on an exception the loop still sleeps and retries — good resilience. Startup `await asyncio.sleep(5)` is fine.
`PATCH /api/customers/{cid}` uses CustomerIn which has required `name`; using Optional-friendly model would allow partial updates. Not blocking.
`list_users` returns admin to staff — intentional for name lookup; confirm with product.
seed_data_creation: Tests created customers prefixed 'TEST_', a category 'TEST_HoodCleaning', jobs titled 'TEST_Job1/2/ToCancel', and a user 'test_newstaff@kgvac.com' (now disabled). Seed admin/staff users and seed categories (Grease Trap Cleaning, Drain Cleaning, Other) are created by the backend lifespan.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_kgvac_backend.py and must be invoked with `pytest -n 0` (override the `-n 2 --dist loadscope` set in /app/backend/pytest.ini) because tests share module-level STATE across classes. Alternative: refactor into class-scoped fixtures that reauthenticate per class, then default pytest.ini addopts will work. Use BASE_URL from env EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. The test suite creates persistent data (TEST_ prefixed); re-running is idempotent (duplicate-user test skips if already created, status transitions tolerate re-runs because each run creates new jobs).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs discovered. Initial parallel-run failures were caused by pytest-xdist loadscope distributing classes across workers while the test suite relied on module-level STATE sharing. Workaround: `-n 0`.
